title: Probe (borg-agent/probe@1)
description: One question, answered in counted trials (R3, mode C). A probe is data: this document says what is asked, how the situation is made, which action is tried against which control, which seeds are declared before it runs, and what counts as a success. Running it plays one trial per seed per arm; the result is 'quantified N of M', written by the harness and never by a model (R4.3). A setup built with the game's debug commands is an intervention, marked as such and kept out of survival figures (decision D4).

id.description: The probe's name, and the id its claim and its result are filed under. A probe file edited after it has a result is a new probe with a new id.

question.description: The one question, in a line. 'Can a level-1 Warrior melee a floating eye and live?'

statement.description: The claim's statement, if the answer should be phrased differently from the question. The question is used when it is absent.

scope.description: What the answer is about, in the claim's own vocabulary (R4): the class, race, character level, depth, gear and version it holds for.

kind.description: 'natural': found in deterministic play, so the trial counts in survival figures. 'intervened': built with the game's own debug commands, marked as an intervention and kept out of them (D4).

take_over_at.description: The game turn the agent takes over at, with the Borg playing the prefix (BORG_AGENT_FROM_TURN, as mode B does). Absent means from birth.

steps.description: The debug commands that build the situation, in order, each typed as a person types it: the debug prefix, the command's own letter from the game's debug table, and the answer to its prompt. Only for an intervened setup.

monster.description: For 'summon': the monster's name as lib/gamedata/monster.txt spells it.

depth.description: For 'depth': the level to jump to.

expect.description: What the game must show before the action is tried. A trial that never sees it is `setup_failed` and counted apart -- never as a trial the character survived.

monster_adjacent.description: A monster of this name, next to the player.

action.description: The action under test, tried every decision once the situation is there.

control.description: The other thing the character could do, played on the same seeds. Without it a count says how often the character lived, not whether the action mattered.

seeds.description: Declared here before the probe runs, and named in the result, so a probe cannot be run again until it gives the answer someone wanted.

success.description: The predicate, mechanical and decided from the run: 'survived' is any end but death; 'killed_it_and_lived' also asks that the monster is gone from the last observation.

notes.description: Anything a reader of the result needs to know about how the question was put.

then.description: An intervened setup says what it does to the game.

arm.description: One thing to try: an executor primitive, or a single game command. Exactly one of them.
